text:
It may have been the longest buildup in world football. In June the former Barcelona and Brazil legend Ronaldinho was unveiled by Italian Serie C side Ravenna, to make his comeback at the age of 46 – 11 years after his last official game. Then silence.
But on a chilly November day on the eastern coast of Italy, there he was, not only in the squad but in the starting XI for the eagerly anticipated derby against Forlì as Ravenna chase promotion to Serie B.
The Ravenna manager, Andrea Mandorlini, deployed Ronaldinho in a central position, just behind the striker Simone Rabbi. The Brazilian held his position well but was slow to get going. As the game progressed, he warmed up and showed his excellent skills; some things do not appear to change. Ronaldinho had 25 ball touches, took three corners – one of which nearly led to a Ravenna goal – and initiated the move that led to the hosts taking the lead in the 35th minute.
Having trained with the team just once, whether he plays again remains to be seen. But he had already sprinkled some magic on a club and a region that has not made headlines in years. He played the first half as Ravenna won 2-0 to stay second in the division’s Group B (the Italian third tier is divided into three regional sections). Only the group winners earn promotion and Ravenna currently trail Spezia by six points.
Whatever happens for the remainder of the season this has put the club back on the football map. Ravenna’s highest-ever finish was eighth in Serie B, back in 1996-97. Yet this match was broadcast live by Sky Sports in Italy and shown in several other countries. It even appeared on the giant screens in New York’s Times Square, where the club’s owners, the Cipriani family, have built much of their international reputation through Harry’s Bar.
The town’s mayor, Alessandro Barattoni, who, as always, was watching the game from the stands, said: “A champion like Ronaldinho, a world football icon, brings great visibility and today is an opportunity for us to showcase Ravenna around the world, from our stadium. It is something new for us and together with the club the municipality will try to understand how this can have a positive impact on the town.”
The local community had been excited at the prospect of Ronaldinho representing the club, but there was some regret too, that he had not been around much. “It would have been nice if he had come to take a stroll around the city, among the people who live here and own the shops,” the barista Barbara says before the game.
So how did he end up here? The Brazilian is a friend of Ignazio Cipriani, the owner of the Giallorossi. Lorenzo Tonetti and Ariedo Braida, old acquaintances from Ronaldinho’s time at Milan, are also part of the club. They convinced him to become an investor in the club and to pull on his boots again. In addition they are now wearing his R10 sportswear line and one of the stands bears the same name.
Ravenna are aiming high. Cipriani has never hidden the fact that he is aiming for Serie A, which is ambitious for a city with a population of 156,000. And Sunday brought hope, Dinho stepping on to the pitch in a gold-trimmed kit picked by the club to celebrate his arrival (and, coincidentally, available for sale at €120). His trademark hair was kept in check by a black headband and he was wearing gloves on the chilly afternoon. On his back, the No 10, something more than just a number for him, the man who became a global icon thanks to his extraordinary skill and contagious smile.
A younger generation has been able to discover Ronaldinho’s genius through the endless supply of online videos showcasing his greatest moments. Children who have never seen him play know his tricks and signature moves, while their parents can relive an era of football they feel no longer exists.
“Dad, was he strong?” a young girl asked her father as they walked hand in hand towards the stadium. “Yes, he was strong. Actually, he is strong!” he corrected himself.
One family had left Rome at 5am and travelled the 350km north just because their son had watched Ronaldinho on YouTube and declared he wanted to see him live. Others had travelled even further, with supporters arriving from Turkey and Canada.
Ronaldinho had, before the weekend, scored 299 professional goals and most screenwriters would have scripted him reaching his landmark 300th on his return, but it was not to be. However, in front of a record attendance of 6,743 the way he initiated the move for Giulio Donati’s goal was ample reward for those who had turned up. Remarkably, Donati made his Serie A debut on 29 August 2010 for Lecce, at San Siro, against Milan, marking the Brazilian that day.
As Ronaldinho walked off at half-time, he was surrounded by a media scrum. Afterwards, he spoke ofhis desire to play again. “It’s true, it all went by too quickly,” he said. “Football is like that, it’s always been like that for me.” And who knows, perhaps he enjoyed himself so much that he wants to extend his career even further. “I don’t know but if the president calls me, I’ll come back. It’s always a pleasure to play, I told him: ‘when he needs me, I’m there’.”
Mandorlini was effusive too. “We’re here and we’re truly proud to have been the architects of this match you played in,” he told the Brazilian. “So, if you want to play another one, that’s fine.”
Who knows what the future holds? For now, Ravenna fans will always have this: a day when a true legend connected people from around the world and allowed them, for one afternoon, to dream.
digest_he: כדורגלן העבר הברזילאי רונאלדיניו ערך הופעת בכורה מפתיעה ומרגשת במדי קבוצת רבנה מהליגה השלישית באיטליה בגיל 46. כוכב ברצלונה לשעבר, הפועל גם כמשקיע במועדון, פתח בהרכב למשחק הדרבי מול פורלי לעיני קהל שיא של קือบלהרדים, ושיחק מחצית שלמה לפני שהוחלף. למרות שעלה למגרש לאחר אימון יחיד בלבד עם הקבוצה, הברזילאי הציג ניצוצות מהיכולת הטבעית שלו ואף יזם את המהלך שהוביל לשער הראשון בניצחון 2-0 של קבוצתו. החזרה החד-פעמית או אולי הממושכת למגרשים עוררה הדים עולמיים והביאה חשיפה תקשורתית רבה למועדון השואף להעפיל לליגת המשנה.
